title: Poll a VCF Automation day-2 deployment request to a terminal status
prompt:
Implement `vcfautomation/client.go` as a standard-library-only Go client that runs a day-2 action against a VMware Cloud Foundation Automation 9.1 deployment and follows the resulting asynchronous request to a terminal status. Do not add dependencies or edit any other file.

VCF Automation, the VCF 9.1 successor to vRealize and Aria Automation, publishes no OpenAPI document in the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository, and its Broadcom xAPIs reference pages offer no specification download. The protected `docs/contract.json` is therefore a hand-transcribed projection of Broadcom's rendered VCF Automation reference documentation for the VM Apps Org - Deployment API, and its `x-contract-source` block says so plainly. `docs/official_sources.json` records every reference page URL, the operation each page documents, and the date it was fetched. Use only the three operations the contract names: `getDeploymentActions` (`GET /deployment/api/deployments/{deploymentId}/actions`), `submitDeploymentActionRequest` (`POST /deployment/api/deployments/{deploymentId}/requests`) and `getRequest` (`GET /deployment/api/requests/{requestId}`).

Preserve the supplied public API: `NewClient(baseURL, accessToken string, httpClient *http.Client) (*Client, error)`, `(*Client).RunDeploymentAction(ctx context.Context, deploymentID string, action ActionRequest) (*Request, error)`, the exported `Client.PollInterval` and `Client.PollTimeout` fields, and the types `Action`, `ActionRequest`, `Request`, `APIError`, `ProtocolError`, `RequestFailedError` and `ErrPollTimeout`. A nil HTTP client means `http.DefaultClient`. Reject an empty, unparseable or non-HTTP(S) service-root URL, a blank or header-unsafe access token, a nil context, a blank deployment ID and a blank action name; reject all of these before any request reaches the network. Errors must not disclose the access token.

`RunDeploymentAction` does three things in order. First it reads the deployment's available actions and resolves the `ResourceAction` whose `name` equals `ActionName`; a name the deployment does not expose, an action whose `valid` flag is false, and an action carrying no `id` are each a `*ProtocolError`. Second it submits that action id. Third it polls the returned request.

The `ResourceActionRequest` body always carries the resolved `actionId`. Its other two members are optional and `ActionRequest` uses a nil pointer and a nil map to mean unset. Omit an unset member from the encoded body completely: never serialize it as an empty string, an empty object, `null` or any other placeholder. Preserve an explicitly supplied value even when it is empty, so a non-nil `Reason` pointing at `""` sends `"reason": ""` and a non-nil empty `Inputs` map sends `"inputs": {}`. A submit response carrying no `id` is a `*ProtocolError`, because the request cannot then be polled.

The submitted request is asynchronous and must be polled rather than assumed complete: poll `getRequest` at least once regardless of the status in the submit response. `SUCCESSFUL` is the successful terminal status; `FAILED`, `ABORTED` and `APPROVAL_REJECTED` are unsuccessful terminal statuses. `CREATED`, `PENDING`, `INITIALIZATION`, `CHECKING_APPROVAL`, `APPROVAL_PENDING`, `USER_INTERACTION_PENDING`, `INPROGRESS` and `COMPLETION` are not terminal and must keep the poll running. Any other value, including an empty one, is outside the contract enum and is a `*ProtocolError` rather than something to guess at. Stop at the first terminal status and do not read it again.

A successful terminal request returns the `*Request` with a nil error. An unsuccessful terminal request returns the terminal `*Request` alongside a `*RequestFailedError` carrying `RequestID`, `Status` and `Details`, so the caller can still inspect it. Every other failure returns a nil `*Request`. Wait `PollInterval` between polls and bound total polling by `PollTimeout`, each falling back to a package default when zero; exhausting the timeout returns an error satisfying `errors.Is(err, ErrPollTimeout)`, and a context that is done returns an error satisfying `errors.Is(err, ctx.Err())`.

Every request carries exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` header and exactly one `Accept: application/json` header. Both GET operations are strictly bodyless: no `Content-Type`, no body, no positive content length and no transfer encoding. The POST carries exactly one `Content-Type: application/json` and a content length equal to its body. No operation in the contract defines a query parameter, so no request may carry a query string or a bare `?`. Escape path variables with normal Go path escaping. Treat only exact HTTP 200 as success; decode a non-200 body's `errorCode` and `message` into `*APIError` with its `StatusCode`, and report a malformed or contract-violating success body as `*ProtocolError`.

Run `go test -race ./...`. The protected verifier is table-driven. It starts the shipped contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port and reads that mock's synchronized in-process request log. It checks the contract's stated reference-documentation provenance, the recorded source pages, the projected routes and status enum, scripted lifecycles that settle in each terminal status, exact poll counts and operation ordering, timeout and cancellation, error mapping, concurrent use, and the exact request wire shape including complete omission of every unset optional body member. The mock builds its routes from `docs/contract.json` and serves no operation absent from that contract. Verification never contacts a live VMware endpoint.

source_basis.api_name: VCF Automation API - VM Apps Org - Deployment

specification_repository.note: VCF Automation ships no OpenAPI document in vmware/vcf-api-specs, so docs/contract.json is transcribed from the rendered xAPIs reference pages instead of extracted from a published specification.

scenario: A day-2 deployment action is resolved by name, submitted, and then polled through the documented non-terminal statuses, including COMPLETION and the approval states, until the request settles in SUCCESSFUL, FAILED, ABORTED or APPROVAL_REJECTED.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves the exact ResourceActionRequest wire shape, including complete omission of every unset optional member rather than an empty, null or default representation, alongside exact poll counts that forbid treating the submit response as terminal.
